reading: Ice versus water is the biggest switch. For 65 of 85 genomes the main axis of within-genome variation separates ice from water, more than winter (12) or pool (8). After dosing, ice and water states differ significantly in 52 of 60 testable genomes in 2024-25 and 44 of 47 in 2025-26. The same population behaves differently in brine than in the water below.

Sulfurimonas differs between pools, but not because of diesel. semibin_088 has one of the strongest pool separations (R² 0.48), yet the diesel-pool water moved less from its own pre-dosing state than the control did (shift 0.5×). The pools carry different strains of this genome (see Sulfur & hydrogen), which this method cannot tell apart from physiology. Along PC1 it trades ribosomal proteins (r +0.93) against motility and chemotaxis (r -0.95), and it slides from the growth end to the motile end through the 2025-26 season in both pools (growth index 98→38‰ diesel, 115→27‰ control).

Cycloclasticus lorbin_184 slows as its bloom ages. Its growth index falls over the 2025-26 diesel season (67→44‰). Its main axis sets hydrocarbon-degradation genes (r -0.76) and storage (r -0.53) against chaperones and proteases (r +0.70). Diesel-pool samples do not drift steadily along it (r -0.08 with day); it separates ice from water instead (R² 0.46). The slowdown with time shows in the growth index rather than in a steady shift of the whole profile.

The 2024-25 Cycloclasticus (metabat_9342) moves between growth and scavenging. Its PC1 sets ribosomal proteins (r -0.66) and cold-shock proteins (r -0.78) against motility (r +0.63), transporters (r +0.71), storage (r +0.83) and nitrogen acquisition (r +0.87): a fast-growth state versus a foraging, nutrient-limited state.

50-400-T64 is still in growth mode at the end. Its growth index rises slightly over the 2025-26 diesel season (69→81‰), consistent with its late bloom (see the 50-400-T64 page). Its main axis pairs chaperones (r -0.72), oxidative-stress (r -0.78) and cold-shock genes against transporters (r +0.76) and nitrogen acquisition (r +0.84).

Background heterotrophs slow down in the diesel pool. Two abundant genomes that do not eat diesel lose growth-index share in the diesel pool but not in the control in 2025-26: Sulfitobacter metabat_5376 (137→96‰ diesel, 160→157‰ control; shift 1.1×, R² 0.11, q = 0.0014) and UBA9145 vamb_4149 (81→52‰ diesel, 74→80‰ control). In UBA9145, phage-shock (psp) genes load strongly on PC1 (r +0.81), the same envelope-stress response seen on the Metals & toxicity page.

What this cannot do. Genomes that are abundant in only one pool (the blooming Cycloclasticus and 50-400-T64) cannot be compared between pools, because the control has too few reads on them. A MAG can hide several strains, and different strains in different pools or winters look like different states. Nitrosopumilus had too few reads for a profile. One pool per treatment, so no test separates diesel from other pool differences.
